paragraphs: VQShape addresses a problem with general-purpose time-series models: their internal representations can support predictions without explaining what patterns they encode. The paper introduces a pretrained model that connects its learned representation to recognizable shapes in a time series, making representation learning and classification more interpretable.

The central mechanism is vector quantization, which describes data using a shared collection of compact codes. In VQShape, each code has a corresponding abstract shape in the time domain. This gives the representation a concrete interpretation: different time series can be expressed through a common vocabulary of shapes, even when they come from different domains.

The authors show that these representations support interpretable classifiers with performance comparable to specialist models. They also report zero-shot transfer of the model and its codebook to datasets and domains absent from pretraining. Together, these findings suggest that a reusable representation can preserve meaningful shape information while supporting classification across the evaluated domains.
neurips-2024-abstracted-shapes-as-tokens.tldr: VQShape represents time series through a shared vocabulary of interpretable shapes that supports classification and zero-shot transfer.

paragraphs: ConStat approaches benchmark contamination through its effect on measured ability. Instead of defining contamination solely as benchmark examples appearing in training data, the paper defines it as artificially elevated benchmark performance that fails to generalize. This shifts the focus toward whether a reported score reflects capability beyond the particular evaluation.

The method compares performance on a primary benchmark with performance on a reference benchmark, using a collection of reference models to interpret the relationship. Relevant checks can involve rephrased questions, synthetic examples from the same distribution, or another benchmark covering the same task. The statistical comparison is designed to both detect contamination and quantify its impact.

The authors evaluate ConStat across different architectures, benchmarks, and contamination scenarios. They report substantial contamination in evaluated models from the Mistral, Llama, and Yi families, as well as the three leading Open LLM Leaderboard models in their study. These findings concern inflated, non-generalizing performance under the paper's definition, making transfer between evaluations central to interpreting benchmark scores.
neurips-2024-constat-performance-based-c.tldr: ConStat detects and quantifies benchmark contamination by testing whether unusually strong performance carries over to related evaluations.

paragraphs: COSMIC addresses the mismatch between the volume of satellite imagery being collected and the capacity available to transmit it to Earth. Learned compression can reduce transmission demands, but sophisticated image encoders are difficult to run on satellites with limited computing power and energy. The paper therefore divides the work according to where resources are constrained.

A lightweight encoder compresses images aboard the satellite, reducing its computational operation count by a factor of 2.5 to 5. Simplifying the encoder weakens its ability to extract image features, so COSMIC uses a diffusion model during reconstruction on the ground to compensate for lost detail. Sensor information, including coordinates and observation time, provides conditions for that reconstruction.

The approach treats satellite observations as images accompanied by useful contextual information. This allows the ground-side model to draw on more than the compressed visual representation alone. The reported experiments outperform leading comparison methods on both perceptual and distortion measures, supporting the effectiveness of combining economical onboard encoding with richer ground-side reconstruction.
neurips-2024-cosmic-compress-satellite-i.tldr: COSMIC combines lightweight satellite image compression with ground-based diffusion reconstruction conditioned on sensor information.

paragraphs: DiP-GO aims to reduce the cost of image generation with diffusion models, whose repeated denoising stages require substantial computation. Conventional pruning can demand expensive retraining, while simple strategies for reusing similar features across neighboring stages leave potential savings unexplored. The paper turns the choice of computations to retain into an optimization problem.

The method first expands a standard diffusion model into a SuperNet by adding backup connections based on similarities between features. A separate pruner network and specially designed losses then identify redundant computation. A small number of gradient optimization steps, followed by post-processing, selects a smaller SubNet from the available computational paths.

The authors test the approach on several diffusion models, including Stable Diffusion variants and diffusion transformers. For SD-1.5, they report a 4.4-fold speedup without accuracy loss in their evaluation, outperforming prior methods. This result supports learning how to remove redundant work across denoising stages, rather than relying only on fixed rules for exploiting feature similarity.
neurips-2024-dip-go-a-diffusion-pruner-v.tldr: DiP-GO learns which diffusion computations to remove, reporting a 4.4-fold SD-1.5 speedup without accuracy loss in its evaluation.

paragraphs: GeSS provides a benchmark for evaluating geometric deep learning when scientific data change between training and testing. Models that handle geometric structure well still need to work under distribution shifts, and the paper identifies this as an underexplored part of their evaluation. Its contribution is a structured collection of settings for examining that problem.

The benchmark spans particle physics, materials science, and biochemistry. It includes conditional, covariate, and concept shifts, giving researchers several kinds of change to investigate. It also distinguishes three information conditions: no access to out-of-distribution data, access to unlabeled examples, and access to examples with a small number of labels.

Combining these dimensions produces 30 experimental settings, each evaluating three geometric model backbones and eleven learning algorithms. This design supports comparisons that account for both the scientific setting and the information available for adaptation. The paper analyzes the resulting evaluations to inform researchers and practitioners considering geometric learning for applications where training and deployment data may differ.
neurips-2024-gess-benchmarking-geometric.tldr: GeSS benchmarks geometric deep learning across scientific domains, distribution shifts, and different levels of access to shifted data.

paragraphs: This paper studies how softmax attention supports in-context learning for regression tasks. In this setting, a model receives examples of a new task during inference and must predict within that context without further training. The analysis asks what kind of prediction rule an attention unit learns from its pretraining tasks.

The authors show that the unit learns a neighborhood window and uses it to implement a nearest-neighbors predictor. The window reflects properties of the pretraining tasks: it becomes wider when their functions vary less sharply, expressed as lower Lipschitzness, and when their labels contain more noise. The learned rule therefore adapts how broadly it draws on nearby examples.

For low-rank linear problems, the attention unit also learns to project inputs into the appropriate subspace before inference. The analysis attributes these adaptive behaviors crucially to the softmax activation; the linear activation considered in earlier theoretical work cannot reproduce them in this setting. The findings give a specific account of how attention can acquire a task-sensitive prediction mechanism through pretraining.
neurips-2024-in-context-learning-with-tr.tldr: In the studied regression setting, softmax attention learns a nearest-neighbors prediction window adapted to task smoothness and label noise.

paragraphs: InfiNet explores an architectural question beyond the usual focus on making networks wider or deeper: how richly can their features interact? The paper distinguishes the size of a feature representation from the space of relationships that can be expressed between features. Its goal is to expand this interaction space.

Element-wise multiplication already offers a way to model interactions, but the authors argue that commonly used multiplications mainly capture low-order relationships within finite-dimensional spaces. InfiNet instead introduces an RBF kernel, drawing on classical kernel methods to enable interactions in an infinite-dimensional space. The architectural change concerns how features combine, rather than merely increasing their number.

The authors report state-of-the-art experimental performance and attribute the improvement to these richer interactions. The stated finding supports feature interaction as a useful direction for model design alongside representation capacity. Here, infinite dimensionality describes the interaction space created by the kernel; the paper's contribution is an architecture that brings this form of interaction into a neural model.
neurips-2024-infinite-dimensional-featur.tldr: InfiNet uses an RBF kernel to expand feature interactions into an infinite-dimensional space and reports improved experimental performance.

paragraphs: SelfClean addresses errors inside image benchmarks that can distort estimates of model performance. The paper considers three kinds of problems: images unrelated to the dataset's subject, near-duplicate examples, and incorrect labels. It frames cleaning as a systematic auditing task, with outputs suited to either human review or automated decisions.

In the ranking formulation, suspicious examples are ordered so that people can concentrate their inspection effort. In the scoring formulation, decisions can be made from the distribution of issue scores. Both rely on a combination of context-aware, self-supervised representations and distance-based indicators, which the authors find effective for identifying problems without annotation biases.

The method exceeds prior detection performance on benchmarks including ImageNet-1k, Food-101N, and STL-10, covering both deliberately introduced issues and existing contamination. Across the audited benchmarks, the authors identify issue levels reaching 16% and confirm more reliable evaluation after cleaning. The contribution therefore connects finding problematic examples with improving the trustworthiness of the benchmark measurements themselves.
neurips-2024-intrinsic-self-supervision-.tldr: SelfClean uses self-supervised representations and distance-based indicators to find image dataset issues and improve evaluation reliability.

paragraphs: MECD introduces a task and dataset for reasoning about causal relationships across multiple events in long videos. Existing tasks, as characterized by the paper, focus mainly on questions about short videos with simple event structures. MECD instead asks for an organized event-level diagram explaining how earlier events relate to a final outcome.

The input includes visual segments and textual event descriptions. The proposed framework uses an event prediction model inspired by Granger causality: it compares predictions of the result event when earlier events are visible versus masked. These differences provide estimates of causal associations. The framework also incorporates front-door adjustment and counterfactual inference to address confounding and misleading causal relationships.

The experiments support the framework's effectiveness at identifying relationships in videos containing multiple events. The authors report improvements of 5.7% over GPT-4o and 4.1% over VideoLLaVA. The contribution combines a broader evaluation task with a concrete prediction-and-masking procedure for constructing structured causal explanations, moving beyond isolated answers about individual video events.
neurips-2024-mecd-unlocking-multi-event-.tldr: MECD introduces structured causal reasoning across long videos and a masking-based framework that estimates relationships between events.

paragraphs: This paper investigates why large vision-language models sometimes describe objects in ways unsupported by their image inputs. Its pilot study links this behavior to Rotary Position Encoding, or RoPE, which models positional relationships between tokens. The authors observe more hallucination when relevant visual information lies farther from instruction tokens in the input sequence.

Their tests suggest that RoPE's decay over long distances makes these visual-instruction relationships harder to capture. Reversing the order of visual tokens during multimodal alignment produces a similar effect, further connecting token arrangement with the observed problem. The proposed Concentric Causal Attention strategy changes positional alignment to reduce relative distances between visual and instruction tokens.

By bringing those tokens closer in the positional representation, the method aims to improve their interaction and strengthen image-grounded responses. The authors report substantial gains over existing hallucination mitigation strategies on multiple object hallucination benchmarks. These results support positional alignment as a useful intervention for the studied hallucination behavior, grounded in the observed distance-related weakness of RoPE.
neurips-2024-mitigating-object-hallucina.tldr: Concentric Causal Attention reduces visual-instruction token distances to mitigate RoPE-related object hallucination in vision-language models.

paragraphs: OccFusion tackles human rendering from videos in which obstructions hide parts of the body. The paper identifies full visibility as a restrictive assumption in existing approaches, because real scenes often provide only partial observations. Its method combines a 3D Gaussian representation with guidance from pretrained 2D diffusion models to complete and render the person.

The pipeline has three stages. Initialization generates complete human masks from masks covering only visible regions. Optimization then adjusts the 3D human Gaussians, using additional guidance from Score-Distillation Sampling to build complete geometry. Refinement applies in-context inpainting to improve the appearance of body regions that have been observed less.

Each stage addresses a different part of incomplete observation: the person's extent, their geometry, and the visual quality of less-seen regions. Evaluations on ZJU-MoCap and challenging OcMotion sequences show state-of-the-art results for rendering occluded people. The findings support combining efficient 3D Gaussian splatting with generative guidance when the input video cannot directly supply a complete view of the body.
neurips-2024-occfusion-rendering-occlude.tldr: OccFusion combines 3D Gaussian splatting and diffusion guidance to reconstruct and render people despite partial visibility.

paragraphs: This paper asks whether collecting more demonstrations and fine-tuning language models can be enough to build reliable agents that operate user interfaces. To investigate, the authors introduce AndroidControl, a dataset containing 15,283 demonstrations of everyday Android app tasks. It covers 14,548 distinct tasks across 833 apps, providing substantial variety for studying generalization.

Each task includes both high-level and low-level human instructions. This lets the study examine performance at different levels of task complexity, alongside whether evaluation examples belong to the training domain or fall outside it. The dataset therefore supports analysis of both data scale and the demands placed on the agent.

Within the training domain, fine-tuned models outperform zero-shot and few-shot baselines, with scaling trends suggesting that more demonstrations might plausibly deliver robust performance. Outside that domain, improvements arrive substantially more slowly. For high-level tasks in particular, the results suggest that additional fine-tuning data alone may be insufficient. The findings distinguish promising scaling within familiar settings from the harder challenge of broader transfer.
neurips-2024-on-the-effects-of-data-scal.tldr: AndroidControl shows promising data scaling for familiar UI tasks, while robust performance outside the training domain may require more than additional fine-tuning data.

paragraphs: OSEDiff uses pretrained diffusion models to improve low-quality images in a single diffusion step. Many existing methods begin with random noise and repeatedly reconstruct an image under guidance from the input. The paper targets both the computational cost of that repeated process and the output uncertainty introduced by sampling the initial noise.

Its starting point is the low-quality image itself, which already contains substantial information about the desired reconstruction. The authors adapt the pretrained network through trainable layers to handle complex degradation. They also use variational score distillation in the latent representation to impose KL-divergence regularization, helping the one-step model produce high-quality outputs.

Starting from the image removes the uncertainty associated specifically with random-noise initialization. In experiments, OSEDiff delivers comparable or better results than earlier diffusion-based methods requiring dozens or hundreds of steps, according to both objective measures and subjective evaluations. The findings support retaining the input's information throughout reconstruction while using the pretrained diffusion model's generative capabilities with much less iterative computation.
neurips-2024-one-step-effective-diffusio.tldr: OSEDiff starts from the low-quality image and uses one diffusion step to achieve results comparable to or better than evaluated multistep methods.

paragraphs: OCTree uses large language models to generate useful features for prediction from tables. The paper identifies two restrictions in existing automated feature engineering: dependence on a predefined search space and feedback dominated by validation scores. A score can indicate whether a trial worked, but the proposed approach also seeks to communicate information about the trial's behavior.

The framework asks an LLM to propose feature generation rules without requiring a manually specified search space. It then uses decision trees to express evidence from previous experiments in natural language. That evidence describes the impact of generated features on predictive performance and becomes feedback for the next round of rule improvement.

This creates an iterative process in which feature proposals are informed by earlier experimental outcomes through structured, language-based reasoning. The authors report consistent improvements across multiple prediction models and diverse benchmarks, outperforming competing automated feature engineering methods. The findings support decision trees as a way to convey useful experimental feedback to an LLM that is helping design tabular features.
neurips-2024-optimized-feature-generatio.tldr: OCTree uses decision-tree feedback to help LLMs iteratively generate better features for tabular prediction.

paragraphs: This paper studies federated learning for clients that must make predictions as new data arrive and conditions change. Much previous work assumes fixed local training datasets, whereas streaming environments require continuing adaptation. A pretrained model can become poorly matched to evolving observations, creating a reason to fine-tune it online.

The proposed algorithm gives each client a personalized mixture containing its locally fine-tuned model and several federated models learned by the server over time. This combines adaptation to the client's own observations with models produced through collaboration. Clients retain their data locally rather than sending their raw datasets to the coordinating server.

The motivation includes an unresolved question in earlier analyses: when does participating in federated online fine-tuning help beyond local fine-tuning alone? The authors provide theoretical analysis and experiments on real datasets supporting their approach for real-time prediction and federated model updating. Its distinctive contribution is to make personalization depend on both ongoing local learning and a collection of shared models accumulated over time.
neurips-2024-personalized-federated-lear.tldr: The method personalizes streaming predictions by mixing a locally adapted model with multiple federated models learned over time.

paragraphs: Optical neural networks offer low latency, low power use, and parallel computation, but physical implementations can perform worse than ideal simulations. This paper investigates that gap through image classification experiments. It identifies two measurable sources of degraded predictions: instability in the light source and mismatches in exposure time.

The proposed learning framework addresses these effects through several coordinated components. A specially designed loss reduces sensitivity to light fluctuations, while a CCD adjustment strategy addresses exposure mismatches. An additional compensation network uses physical prior knowledge to handle other systematic errors. Together, these components aim to align light intensity behavior between simulations and physical experiments.

The reported MNIST accuracy rises from 61.6% for the original optical network to 96.5% with the framework. Accuracy also increases from 63.0% to 85.7% on QuickDraw16 and from 56.2% to 77.5% on Fashion MNIST. Comparisons with leading optical approaches further support the method, showing that explicitly addressing physical system errors can substantially improve the evaluated hardware's classification performance.
neurips-2024-physics-constrained-compreh.tldr: A physics-constrained framework improves optical neural network accuracy by compensating for light instability, exposure mismatch, and other system errors.

paragraphs: QGym provides a simulation framework for studying how controllers allocate limited resources across queues. Such decisions matter in settings including manufacturing, communications, and healthcare. Queueing problems pose distinctive difficulties: events unfold in continuous time, outcomes are highly random, and poor control over long periods can produce rapidly growing delays.

The framework supplies a modular collection of environments, including parallel servers, criss-cross networks, tandem networks, and re-entrant networks. It also includes a hospital queueing system calibrated to realistic conditions. Researchers can extend these initial instances and use them to test both model-free reinforcement learning policies and classical queueing control methods.

The contribution is a broader empirical testbed for controller development and comparison. Mathematical guarantees in idealized settings remain useful, but QGym adds a way to examine behavior across varied, more realistic problem instances. Its design makes the system structure and practical operating challenges part of the evaluation, supporting investigation of controllers under the stochastic, long-horizon conditions that characterize queueing networks.
neurips-2024-qgym-scalable-simulation-an.tldr: QGym supplies modular queueing simulations for comparing reinforcement learning and classical controllers across varied, realistic settings.

paragraphs: QuanTA introduces a method for adapting pretrained language models efficiently while allowing high-rank changes. Its motivation is that low-rank approximations, such as those used by LoRA, may be insufficient for complicated downstream tasks. The paper seeks a way to represent richer adaptations without giving up the efficiency benefits of training relatively few parameters.

The method draws on structures inspired by quantum circuits to construct tensor adaptations. A universality theorem and a rank representation theorem provide theoretical support for its ability to express efficient high-rank updates. The authors describe the method as straightforward to implement and report that it adds no overhead during inference.

Experiments show improved commonsense reasoning, arithmetic reasoning, and scalability compared with traditional methods. The paper also reports stronger performance with fewer trainable parameters than competing approaches. QuanTA can additionally be designed to work with existing fine-tuning algorithms. These findings support high-rank adaptation as a practical option when restricting updates to low rank may constrain downstream performance.
neurips-2024-quanta-efficient-high-rank-.tldr: QuanTA uses quantum-inspired tensor structures for parameter-efficient high-rank language model adaptation without added inference overhead.

paragraphs: BeTop addresses the difficulty of keeping predictions and driving plans consistent when multiple road users interact. Uncertainty and different kinds of interaction can make collective behavior unstable when prediction and planning are combined. The paper introduces a representation of shared behavioral structure to guide the trajectories generated downstream.

Behavioral Topology, or BeTop, draws on braid theory to extract interaction patterns from the future trajectories of multiple agents. These patterns supervise BeTopNet, a learning framework that coordinates behavioral prediction and planning using the resulting topology priors. The method also uses imitative contingency learning to handle uncertainty in the behaviors relevant to both tasks.

The authors report state-of-the-art prediction and planning results on large-scale real-world datasets, including nuPlan and WOMD. Additional evaluation on their proposed interactive-scenario benchmark demonstrates planning compliance in interactive cases. The findings support representing the relationships among agents' possible movements as an explicit intermediate structure, so that trajectory generation can follow a more consistent account of how those agents interact.
neurips-2024-reasoning-multi-agent-behav.tldr: BeTop represents multi-agent interaction patterns through topology to improve consistency between autonomous driving prediction and planning.

paragraphs: This paper tackles the difficulty of recognizing human actions from skeleton sequences when evaluation moves to a different dataset. Its central observation is that datasets often capture different portions of an action, creating temporal mismatch. The proposed augmentation framework first recovers a more complete action and then samples new sequences from it.

The recovery procedure uses two kinds of knowledge shared across action examples. Boundary poses help determine an action's start, while linear temporal transforms describe broader action patterns. Both are learned efficiently through clustering over the dataset. Completion then proceeds stochastically through boundary-conditioned extrapolation followed by smooth linear transformations.

Resampling the completed sequences creates training variations intended to prepare the model for unseen domains with different temporal coverage. The authors connect this approach to observed patterns of per-frame diversity over time in large datasets. Evaluation across three skeleton action datasets shows a considerable improvement over other domain generalization methods, supporting action completeness as a useful basis for augmentations that transfer between datasets.
neurips-2024-recovering-complete-actions.tldr: Recovering and resampling complete skeleton actions improves cross-dataset recognition by addressing differences in temporal coverage.

paragraphs: SOFO is an optimizer for recurrent neural networks used as models of brain dynamics. These models face plausibility constraints that can rule out architectural changes commonly used to simplify machine learning training. Their loss surfaces can also be difficult to optimize, while long task horizons make backpropagation demanding in GPU memory.

The method uses second-order optimization with batched forward-mode differentiation, avoiding backpropagation. Its memory cost remains constant with respect to the time horizon. Although many second-order methods contain operations that are inherently sequential, SOFO is designed to exploit GPU parallelism, keeping its per-iteration runtime approximately comparable to first-order gradient-based optimizers.

The authors report substantially better performance than Adam across several recurrent-network tasks. These include a difficult double-reaching motor task and learning an adaptive Kalman filter over a long horizon. The results support changing the optimization procedure as a way to train challenging neuroscience models while preserving their architectural constraints, with the memory behavior particularly relevant to tasks extending over many time steps.
neurips-2024-second-order-forward-mode-o.tldr: SOFO trains neuroscience RNNs using parallel forward-mode second-order optimization with memory cost constant in the time horizon.

paragraphs: This paper studies reinforcement learning with explicit constraints on risk, aiming to reduce the likelihood of severe outcomes. Such constraints are difficult to optimize because risk measures are nonlinear. The proposed method, spectral-risk-constrained policy optimization, or SRCPO, addresses this difficulty for constraints expressed through spectral risk measures.

SRCPO uses a two-level optimization structure built from a dual representation of those risk measures. The outer problem adjusts the associated dual variables. For each choice of those variables, the inner problem seeks an optimal policy. This separates the treatment of the risk measure from policy optimization while keeping them linked through the two-level procedure.

The authors establish convergence to an optimum in the tabular setting and describe this as the first such guarantee to their knowledge. They also evaluate the method on continuous-control tasks, where it performs best among the compared risk-constrained algorithms that satisfy the constraints. The theoretical guarantee applies to the tabular setting, while the continuous-control results provide separate empirical support for the approach.
neurips-2024-spectral-risk-safe-reinforc.tldr: SRCPO uses bilevel optimization for spectral-risk constraints, with optimal convergence in the tabular setting and strong continuous-control results.

paragraphs: Speculative decoding accelerates language model inference by having a draft model propose tokens that the main model then accepts or rejects. Its usefulness depends on two factors: how quickly proposals are produced and how often they are accepted. This paper focuses on improving acceptance by making draft sequences more coherent.

The authors identify a weakness in commonly used non-autoregressive draft models: they generate several future positions quickly but do not adequately account for correlations between the proposed tokens. Their CTC-based draft model strengthens those relationships during drafting. The intended result is a higher-quality candidate sequence that the main model can accept more frequently.

Experiments show higher acceptance rates and faster inference than strong comparison methods. These findings demonstrate the practical importance of draft quality alongside raw drafting speed. A proposal mechanism that accounts more effectively for relationships within the sequence can improve the overall decoding process because the main model accepts more of the work supplied by its draft model.
neurips-2024-speculative-decoding-with-c.tldr: A CTC-based draft model improves token correlations, increasing speculative-decoding acceptance rates and inference speed in experiments.

paragraphs: This paper investigates when gradient descent can successfully train a Transformer and which architectural choices and initial conditions support rapid convergence. The analysis focuses on the loss landscape of a single Transformer layer. It compares two attention mechanisms, one using a Softmax kernel and the other using a Gaussian kernel.

The authors show that appropriate weight initialization can allow gradient descent to reach a global optimum with either attention kernel, especially when the input embedding dimension is large. The result ties optimization success to the conditions of the analysis, including initialization and model structure. It provides a theoretical explanation for circumstances in which training can converge successfully.

The comparison also identifies less favorable cases for Softmax attention, where training can reach suboptimal local solutions. Gaussian attention exhibits more favorable behavior in the studied analysis. Empirical experiments support the theoretical findings. Together, the results show why attention design and initialization deserve attention when reasoning about convergence, while keeping the conclusions grounded in the single-layer setting examined by the paper.
neurips-2024-unraveling-the-gradient-des.tldr: A single-layer analysis identifies initialization and attention-kernel conditions supporting Transformer convergence, while exposing possible suboptimal outcomes with Softmax.

paragraphs: This paper studies how accurately noise variance can be estimated in the normal means model when the means are unknown but bounded. Variance is often assumed known in theoretical treatments, although that information may be unavailable in applications. Boundedness provides the identifying assumption under which the paper establishes the best achievable worst-case estimation rate.

For squared error, the sharp minimax rate is (log log n / log n) squared. The proposed estimator achieves this rate by estimating on the order of log n / log log n cumulants, quantities describing properties of the data distribution. A variational representation connects these cumulants to the noise variance, providing the foundation for the estimator.

The authors also prove a matching lower bound through a moment-matching construction. This establishes that the achieved rate is optimal over the stated bounded-means setting, rather than simply an upper bound for one procedure. The contribution therefore supplies both an estimator and a characterization of the fundamental estimation difficulty under this assumption.
neurips-2024-variance-estimation-in-comp.tldr: Under bounded unknown means, the paper establishes the sharp minimax variance-estimation rate and constructs an estimator that achieves it.
